answer: The zenith multiplier is published, charged in cedar, and grove lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 15 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1452 identities would post 2768 proofs and burn roughly 16 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
